hypothesis.name: Sparse symbolic identification with learned closure residual
hypothesis.scientific_question: Is the dominant ROM error caused by an inadequate or non-interpretable nonlinear basis in the latent space, such that enforcing sparsity and physical interpretability of the identified dynamics — while absorbing the remainder in a small learned residual — yields both better generalization and a falsifiable, inspectable model?
hypothesis.mechanism: A sparse symbolic/linear-combination mode is identified on the latent dynamics (e.g., SINDy-style selection over a candidate library of polynomial, trigonometric, and physically motivated terms), producing an interpretable closed-form component. A small learned network then models the residual closure term that the sparse basis misses. This is mechanistically distinct from C001_H01/H02/H03 which use no-learned symbolic structure; here the dominant dynamics must be expressible in a compact, named basis and the remainder must be genuinely small.
hypothesis.mathematical_form: dz/dt = Ξ^T Θ(z) + R_θ(z), where Ξ is a sparse coefficient matrix identified by sequential thresholded least squares over a library Θ (e.g., {1, z_i, z_i z_j, sin(z_k), ...}), and R_θ is a small neural closure. The sparsity is enforced by hard thresholding or STRRidge; the residual is trained to match (dz/dt − Ξ^T Θ(z)) on data.
hypothesis.motivation: When reduced-order models fail, a common scientific reason is that the chosen basis is too rigid (POD modes miss interactions) or too unstructured (neural networks memorize without generalization). A sparse symbolic identification step provides an inspectable, low-dimensional, physically interpretable skeleton; the closure residual then captures only what the skeleton misses. If the residual turns out to be large, the falsifiable interpretation is that the chosen library is inadequate; if the residual is small and generalization improves, the sparse basis is the right scientific explanation.
hypothesis.explanation_of_previous_failure: C001_H01 relied on a generic delay-embedding map with no symbolic structure; C001_H02 imposed a spatial constraint but left the temporal map generic; C001_H03 split scales but did not require identifiability of the dominant terms. None produced a sparse, named, inspectable form for the dynamics. If the failure is due to an unidentifiable, over-parameterized latent map that does not generalize, a sparse skeleton plus small residual should outperform a pure black box at matched capacity.
hypothesis.distinguishing_prediction: On development_validation the sparse+residual model should (i) yield a sparse Ξ (density below a threshold, e.g., <10% nonzero) with named terms that are scientifically plausible; (ii) achieve lower rollout error than a matched-capacity pure black-box baseline at long horizons; (iii) have a residual norm that is small relative to the sparse-skeleton norm. If the residual is large and the sparse skeleton is dense, the basis is inadequate; if the residual is small but rollout error is not better than the black box, the sparsity itself is not the scientific mechanism.
minimum_experiment: Apply sparse symbolic identification to latent dynamics on development_train to obtain a closed-form component Ξ^T Θ(z).
Train a small residual network on the residual (dz/dt − Ξ^T Θ(z)).
Train a matched-capacity pure black-box baseline on the same prediction target.
Evaluate on development_validation: report rollout MSE, density of Ξ, residual-to-skeleton norm ratio, and qualitative inspection of identified terms.

Falsification criterion: If Ξ is NOT sparse (density ≥ 30%) AND residual norm is comparable to the pure black-box output norm AND rollout MSE is NOT statistically lower than the black-box baseline (paired test, p > 0.05), the sparse-skeleton-plus-residual mechanism is falsified.
hypothesis.expected_observation_if_true: Identified Ξ is sparse with physically meaningful monomials; residual norm is < 50% of skeleton norm; rollout error is lower than matched-capacity black box at long horizons.
hypothesis.expected_observation_if_false: Identified Ξ is dense, residual is comparable to a full nonlinear map, and rollout error matches the black box, indicating the chosen library is inadequate and sparsity is not the bottleneck.
risks: Library selection is itself a modeling choice; an inadequate library will mask the mechanism.
Sparse identification is sensitive to noise and threshold choice; misleading sparsity can occur.
Closure residual may absorb all dynamics if trained without constraints, defeating the sparsity mechanism.
hypothesis.relation_to_existing_methods: Related to SINDy, gray-box modeling, and equation discovery; differs from neural-only latent ROMs (no symbolic skeleton) and from delay-embedding ROMs (no exogenous closure). Distinct from C001_H03 which separated scales but did not require sparse symbolic identifiability.

raw_spec.name: Sparse symbolic identification with learned closure residual
raw_spec.scientific_claim: A dominant fraction of the latent dynamics can be captured by a sparse linear combination of named candidate functions (polynomial and trigonometric features), and a small neural network trained on the residual closure is sufficient to recover the remainder; this yields lower rollout error than a matched-capacity pure black-box map and produces an inspectable, named symbolic skeleton.

hypothesis.motivation: Prior failed candidates used either generic neural maps, generic delay embeddings, or scale-splitting with no symbolic identifiability requirement; if the dominant ROM error comes from an over-parameterized or unidentifiable nonlinear latent map, replacing the mapping with a sparse interpretable skeleton plus a small learned residual should improve generalization and produce a falsifiable model.

representation.normalization: standard score on development_train per latent coordinate; no access to final_test

dynamics.equation: z_next = z_t + dt * ( Xi_T @ Theta(z_t) + R_theta(z_t) )
parameters: Xi (sparse coefficient matrix over candidate library)
Theta (feature library: constant, linear z_i, quadratic z_i*z_j, sin(z_k), cos(z_k))
dt (integration step supplied per environment step)
dynamics.operator_structure: linear-in-parameters symbolic skeleton (SINDy-style thresholded least squares over a fixed named library) plus a small low-capacity nonlinear neural closure; the skeleton is identified first and held fixed, then R_theta is trained on the residual (dz/dt - Xi_T @ Theta(z))
dynamics.stability_mechanism: rollout uses bounded one-step increments with a hard Lipschitz-style clip on R_theta output norm; symbolic skeleton is identified via STLS with hard thresholding so coefficients remain finite; no unstable recurrent unrolling during training

training.loss: stage 1 skeleton: squared error on dz/dt with sparsity-inducing hard threshold; stage 2 residual network: MSE on (dz/dt - Xi_T Theta(z)); combined rollout loss on development_validation for early stopping
training.optimizer: Adam with learning rate 1e-3 for residual MLP; coefficient solver is closed-form ridge for each STLS pass

metrics: rollout MSE on development_validation at horizons 1, 10, 50, 200
residual to skeleton norm ratio: ||R_theta(z)|| / ||Xi_T Theta(z)||
named-term inspection (print which library entries receive nonzero Xi)
paired bootstrap test vs matched-capacity black-box baseline at long horizon
baselines: matched-capacity pure black-box MLP with same parameter count trained on the same dz/dt target

falsification.success_condition: Xi density below 10 percent with physically plausible named terms, residual to skeleton norm ratio below 0.5, and rollout MSE at the long horizon statistically lower than the matched-capacity black-box baseline (paired test p below 0.05)
falsification.failure_condition: Xi density at or above 30 percent AND residual norm comparable to the pure black-box output norm AND rollout MSE not statistically lower than the black-box baseline (paired test p above 0.05)

modules: feature_library.py: builds Theta(z) for constant, linear, quadratic, sin, cos terms given latent_dim
stls.py: sequential thresholded least squares to solve for sparse Xi with configurable threshold
residual_mlp.py: small MLP for R_theta with capacity matched to combined-model parameter budget
combined_model.py: forward dz/dt = Xi_T Theta(z) + R_theta(z) with rollout integrator
matched_blackbox.py: pure MLP baseline with matched parameter count
evaluator.py: rollout MSE, density, norm ratios, paired bootstrap p-value, named-term dump
pseudocode: step 1: load development_train, compute z_t and finite-difference dz/dt targets
step 2: build feature matrix Theta(z_t) using feature_library for all training samples
step 3: solve Xi via STLS: loop regress dz/dt on Theta, threshold small coefficients to zero, repeat until stable; record density and nonzero term indices
step 4: compute skeleton residual r_t = dz/dt_t - Xi_T @ Theta(z_t) on development_train
step 5: train residual_mlp R_theta on (z_t, r_t) using Adam with MSE loss; validate on development_validation for early stopping
step 6: train matched_blackbox on (z_t, dz/dt_t) with identical parameter budget and the same optimizer
step 7: rollout both models autoregressively on development_validation for horizons 1, 10, 50, 200; record rollout MSE
step 8: compute diagnostics: Xi density, ||R_theta(z)|| / ||Xi_T Theta(z)|| ratio, list of named nonzero terms
step 9: paired bootstrap test on rollout MSE at the long horizon between combined model and black-box baseline; report p-value
step 10: emit pass or fail based on falsification criteria
